object.medium: Electronic computer: ECL integrated circuits on hand-wired modules in a Freon-cooled C-shaped cabinet
object.description: The Cray-1 was the first supercomputer built by Seymour Cray's Cray Research and the fastest computer in the world from 1976 to 1982. Its C-shaped tower kept every wire short, and the padded bench around the base hid the power supplies, while liquid Freon carried away the heat of its hand-wired logic. Eighty or more were sold to weapons laboratories, weather centres and universities; this one stands at EPFL in Lausanne.
facts: The first Cray-1 was installed at Los Alamos National Laboratory in 1976, after being announced in 1975.
It ran at an 80 MHz clock (12.5 ns cycle) with 64-bit words and vector registers, and contained over 60 miles of wire, no piece longer than three feet.
Over 80 Cray-1s of all types were sold at $5–8 million each, making Seymour Cray a celebrity and Cray Research a success.
